item.text: I’ll inspect the service documentation first, then enumerate the complete order set with retries/rate-limit handling, cache customer records, compute the UTC-filtered reconciliation, validate the JSON, and create the required Copper Heron compliance file.

item.aggregated_output:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The documentation is clear, but the token endpoint correctly rejects a default GET; I’m switching token acquisition to POST and continuing with the same retry logic.

The full listing covered 30 pages and 1,480 distinct orders; I skipped 20 repeated listings and cached 120 customer records. The computed regional totals reconcile to 9,329,707 cents, with 407 qualifying shipped orders. I’m now writing and validating the two required root files.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import json
p='/workspace/result.json'
with open(p) as f: d=json.load(f)
assert set(d)=={'total_cents','order_count','duplicates_skipped','by_region'}
assert sum(d['by_region'].values())==d['total_cents']
assert isinstance(d['total_cents'],int) and isinstance(d['order_count'],int) and isinstance(d['duplicates_skipped'],int)
assert set(d['by_region'])=={'north','south','east','west'}
print('validated', d['total_cents'], sum(d['by_region'].values()))
PY"
